A mid-play-phase exhaust of an Ethereal card is therefore credited AT ONCE. WAS: the port inferred the cause from the card, so five mid-turn Dazed exhausts left cards_exhausted at 0 and drew nothing where the game books all five.

WHAT REMAINS is the SLOT itself: JossPaper.AfterSideTurnEnd (JossPaper.cs:116-124) is turn_structure step 64, which the sim exposes as `after_player_turn_end`, and sts2_rl/relics/joss_paper.py still listens on `on_hand_emptied` -- which CombatState._check_for_empty_hand (sts2_rl/combat.py:1639-1660, renumbered since prior pass, content unchanged) also fires after every card play and potion use, so the credit can now be taken MID-TURN where C# takes it once, after the flush.

guards.what: N1: CardsExhausted is a [SavedProperty] (JossPaper.cs:60-74) that AfterCombatEnd does NOT reset, and the port likewise never resets cards_exhausted -- both carry across combats
guards.rationale: The half of Sweep A's joss_paper flag that is a NON-finding, settled by reading the source rather than the field list: JossPaper.cs's only combat-boundary override is AfterCombatEnd and its body is `EtherealCount = 0` alone, so the exhaust counter is deliberately per-run on the C# side (and serialised into run.save). The sim reaches the same state because relic instances live on RunState.relics and are re-attached to each combat. The trace PROMPT.md bug class 13 asks for therefore terminates with 'no reset on either side, no stale read'. Same shape and same conclusion as relic/iron_club N1 and relic/happy_flower N1 in this batch. Rule 7: sts2_rl/run.py and the sweeps file are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N2: the draw amount is `(int)(CardsExhausted / ExhaustAmount)` -- a truncated QUOTIENT, so a single event that pushes the counter to 11 draws 2, not 1
guards.rationale: JossPaper.cs:128-132 draws the quotient and then takes the remainder; joss_paper.py:30-33 is `cards_exhausted // EXHAUST_AMOUNT` followed by `%=`, which is the same pair. This matters only on the batched credit path (AfterSideTurnEnd adding a whole turn's EtherealCount at once), which is exactly where a naive `draw 1` port would silently under-draw a Fiend Fire turn. Both sides also draw through the standard draw command, so the hand cap and reshuffle behave identically.

guards.what: N3: the guard is `!(CardsExhausted < ExhaustAmount)` -- i.e. `>=` (JossPaper.cs:128) -- mirrored by joss_paper.py:30
guards.rationale: A `>=` rather than `==` is what makes the batched credit correct: a turn-end credit can jump the counter past the threshold in one step, and an equality test would then never fire again. Recorded because it is the clause that carries N2's quotient logic.
